newsitem.title: USA: NYC receives $112 mln of retail orders for bonds.
newsitem.headline: NYC receives $112 mln of retail orders for bonds.

text.p: New York City on Friday said that it received about $112 million of retail orders for the $626 million of bonds due to sold on Tuesday, as a competing bond sale earlier in the week cut the market's appetite.

A New York City official, who declined to be named, said that the city closed the first two maturities, 2098 and 2099. He did not anticipate changing the price scale. Friday was the second day of the retail order period, which ends at 1200 EST/1700 GMT on Monday.
On Wednesday, the Municipal Assistance Corp for New York City sold $677 million of bonds, which damped interest in the city's own bond sale, the official said.
He added he did not expect to have to reprice New York City's latest offering.
"The market was basically flat so there will be no pricing unless it does something dramatic."
